userStories.title: The REVIEW kind in the protocol and the API model
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the shared REVIEW job model and the API's recoverable bot_review placement gate.

**Motivation** — The fleet design (§9.122, "S6 = K1 + K2") puts the review loop in koda: koda owns the bot identity (the `koda-fleet` App, whose key lives only in koda), triggers reviews, and later (K2) feeds project decisions in and stores review outcomes as memory.

**Approach** — Verbatim API/protocol design requirements (US-008 owns the separate web FleetJobKind change):
- `FleetJobKind` (`apps/api/src/common/enums.ts:143`): adds `REVIEW`.
- `packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts` (types only): `FleetJobKindName` adds `'REVIEW'`; `AssignPayload` adds `review?: { prNumber: number; botLogin: string }`; `RunnerCapabilities` adds `botReview?: true`.
- New `apps/api/src/fleet/common/review-jobs.ts`: `REVIEW_FEATURE_PREFIX = 'review-pr-'`, `reviewFeature(prNumber): string`, `prNumberOfReviewFeature(feature): number | null` (null unless the feature is the prefix followed by a positive safe integer written without a leading zero).
- `parseCapabilitiesCore` (`apps/api/src/fleet/common/capabilities-core.ts`): accepts `botReview: true`, fails `botReview` for any other present value, like `configJobs`.
- Runner capability `botReview?: true`. For a `REVIEW` job, `capabilityMisfit` checks `botReview` first (before profiles, interaction and tools): without it the misfit is `bot_review`, which is not permanent.
- `MisfitReason`, `capabilityMisfit` (`placement-rules.ts`): add `'bot_review'` with the order above.
- Misfit enum lists: `'bot_review'` joins `PlacementMisfitDto`'s enum (`fleet-job.dto.ts:129`) and `MISFIT_REASONS` (`fleet/dashboard/dashboard.types.ts:109`). The job DTO command enum (`fleet-job.dto.ts:51`) adds `'REVIEW'`.

The API may import `@nathapp/fleet-protocol` with `import type` only (`fleet/common/protocol.spec.ts`); runtime helpers are mirrored in the API (`fleet/common/config-jobs.ts`). Protocol edits ride an `apps/api` story, as in `fleet-s5a-thread-core`.

**Implementation connections** — Modify packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts; apps/api/src/common/enums.ts; apps/api/src/fleet/common/capabilities-core.ts; apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/placement-rules.ts; apps/api/src/fleet/dashboard/dashboard.types.ts; apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/dto/fleet-job.dto.ts. Create the local review helpers and co-located unit spec. The exhaustive `Record<FleetJobKindName, true>` named `kinds` in apps/api/src/fleet/common/protocol.spec.ts gains `REVIEW: true` and stays exhaustive over the union. Extend existing capability and placement unit suites. Regenerate openapi.json and the CLI client with `bun run generate` from the repository root; generated source is never hand-edited.

**Scope** — In: protocol types, API kind constants, canonical feature helpers, capability validation, misfit ordering/enum schemas and generation. Out: dispatch request rules (US-002), assignment and budgets (US-003), actual probing (US-004), runner execution (US-005 through US-007), and the web union/rendering change named above (US-008). CLI commands for reviews; the generated CLI client is regenerated but no command is added.

**Interface** — `REVIEW_FEATURE_PREFIX = 'review-pr-'`; `reviewFeature(prNumber): string`; `prNumberOfReviewFeature(feature): number | null`; `review?: { prNumber: number; botLogin: string }`; `botReview?: true`.

userStories.title: Dispatch input rules for REVIEW
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Accept a PR-number-based REVIEW dispatch while retaining RUN/PLAN validation and reserving review feature names.

**Motivation** — The fleet design (§9.122, "S6 = K1 + K2") puts the review loop in koda: koda owns the bot identity (the `koda-fleet` App, whose key lives only in koda), triggers reviews, and later (K2) feeds project decisions in and stores review outcomes as memory.

**Approach** — Verbatim design requirements:
- Fields: `ref` = the repo's default branch; `feature` = `review-pr-<prNumber>`; `planFrom` null; `bashMode` `raw`; `profiles`, `maxCostUsd`, `selectorLabels` and `pinnedRunnerId` from the dispatch body.
- `DispatchFleetJobDto` (`fleet/jobs/dto/dispatch-fleet-job.dto.ts`) — Baseline: `command` `@IsIn(['RUN','PLAN'])`, `feature` required. Target: `@IsIn(['RUN','PLAN','REVIEW'])`; `feature` optional; new optional `prNumber` (integer 1..2147483647).
- `normalizeDispatch(dto, defaultBranch)` (`fleet/jobs/dispatch-input.ts`), reasons in this order:
  - `RUN`/`PLAN`: missing `feature` fails `feature`; a `review-pr-` feature fails `feature is reserved for REVIEW`; a `prNumber` fails `prNumber is only for REVIEW`.
  - `REVIEW`: missing `prNumber` fails `prNumber required for REVIEW`; `feature` fails `feature is derived for REVIEW`; `planFrom` fails `planFrom is only for PLAN`; `ref` fails `ref is the default branch for REVIEW`; a non-raw `bashMode` fails `bashMode must be raw for REVIEW`; non-empty `ticketRefs` fails `ticketRefs is not for REVIEW`. The result has `feature` `reviewFeature(prNumber)` and `ref` = the default branch.

**One active review per PR, through the existing index.** A `REVIEW` job's `feature` is `review-pr-<number>`. The partial unique index `FleetJob_active_repo_feature_key` (`(repoId, feature)` over `QUEUED/ASSIGNED/RUNNING/UPLOADING`) already makes a second active job on one feature a 409. `RUN` and `PLAN` may no longer use a feature that starts with `review-pr-`.

API i18n `fleet.dispatchInput` is `"Invalid dispatch: {reason}"` in both locales, so new reasons need no new key.

**Implementation connections** — Change apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/dto/dispatch-fleet-job.dto.ts and apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/dispatch-input.ts, consuming the US-001 local review helper. Guard the now-optional feature before string operations. Keep existing PLAN planFrom/path restrictions, common profile validation/order, maxCostUsd conversion, bash defaults, approval timeout, label deduplication/sorting and pin propagation. Extend dispatch-input.spec.ts and dto/dispatch-fleet-job.dto.spec.ts. Existing schedule and assistant callers remain RUN/PLAN. Repository contract guidance requires root `bun run generate` when this DTO changes; regenerate rather than manually editing generated clients.

**Scope** — In: transport decorators/types, conditional normalization and specified validation errors. Out: provider-first rejection, route persistence/conflict handling, assignment and budget cancellation (US-003); capability models (US-001); runner parsing/execution (US-005 through US-007); web rendering (US-008). Dispatching a `REVIEW` through the assistant tool `koda_dispatch_job`; its `command` stays `RUN` or `PLAN`.

**Interface** — `@IsIn(['RUN','PLAN','REVIEW'])`; `normalizeDispatch(dto, defaultBranch)`; `reviewFeature(prNumber): string`. New optional `prNumber` is an integer 1..2147483647; feature is optional only at the DTO layer, not for normalized RUN/PLAN jobs.

userStories.title: Dispatching and assigning a REVIEW
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Connect manual GitHub REVIEW dispatch to persisted jobs, identity-bearing assignments and existing budget hard stops.

**Motivation** — The fleet design (§9.122, "S6 = K1 + K2") puts the review loop in koda: koda owns the bot identity (the `koda-fleet` App, whose key lives only in koda), triggers reviews, and later (K2) feeds project decisions in and stores review outcomes as memory.

**Approach** — Verbatim design requirements:
**GitHub only, checked first.** `FleetJobsService.dispatch` rejects a `REVIEW` for a repo whose provider is not `github`, before `normalizeDispatch` runs, with 422 `fleet.dispatchInput` reason `review is GitHub-only`.
- `FleetJobsService.dispatch`: after loading the repo and before `normalizeDispatch`, a `REVIEW` for a non-`github` repo throws `ValidationAppException({ reason: 'review is GitHub-only' }, 'fleet.dispatchInput')`.
- `AssignPayload` gains `review?: { prNumber: number; botLogin: string }`, present only for `REVIEW`; `botLogin` is the `name` of the `GitIdentity` passed to `buildAssignPayload` (for GitHub `<githubAppSlug>[bot]`, fallback `koda-fleet[bot]`).
- `buildAssignPayload`: a `REVIEW` job gains `review: { prNumber: prNumberOfReviewFeature(job.feature), botLogin: gitIdentity.name }`; a `REVIEW` row whose feature does not parse throws `Error('invalid review feature')`.
- `BUDGET_STOP_COMMANDS` (`fleet/budgets/prisma-budget.repository.ts:22`, module-private): adds `REVIEW`.

The runner-cost behavior quoted below is shared design context owned by US-007; US-003 owns the budget command inclusion, not runner cost reading.

**One active review per PR, through the existing index.** A `REVIEW` job's `feature` is `review-pr-<number>`. The partial unique index `FleetJob_active_repo_feature_key` (`(repoId, feature)` over `QUEUED/ASSIGNED/RUNNING/UPLOADING`) already makes a second active job on one feature a 409. `RUN` and `PLAN` may no longer use a feature that starts with `review-pr-`.

**Cost.** A `REVIEW` writes no `status.json`. The runner reports its cost from the nax cost ledger in `<outDir>` with the existing `readPlanCost`, as for `PLAN`. `REVIEW` joins `BUDGET_STOP_COMMANDS`, so a budget hard stop cancels queued reviews like `RUN` and `PLAN`.

**Trust.** koda does not check PR authorship or forks; nax classifies the PR's trust itself.

**Notifications.** A failed `REVIEW` notifies its requester through the existing job-outcome recorder, like any job.

**Failure handling** — A second active REVIEW for the same PR answers 409 from the existing active-feature conflict. With no runner advertising botReview, dispatch answers 201 and the job stays QUEUED with misfit bot_review; a pinned runner lacking botReview also produces 201 because this misfit is recoverable.

**Implementation connections** — Modify apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.ts, apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/assign-payload.ts and apps/api/src/fleet/budgets/prisma-budget.repository.ts. Use US-001 helpers and the US-002 DTO/normalization. Preserve project ownership/not-found handling before the provider check, existing transactional insertion/audit/outbox behavior, DuplicateActiveJobError mapping, CAS placement and transition services. buildAssignPayload's production caller remains placement.service.ts; gitIdentityFor derives the login, not a new App-user lookup. The current kind-agnostic job-outcome recorder already covers ordinary failed REVIEW jobs; do not bypass it. Create apps/api/test/integration/fleet/fleet-review-dispatch.integration.spec.ts using existing HTTP fixtures and shared DB gates; extend assign-payload.spec.ts and the budget-evaluator integration pattern. Regenerate openapi.json and the CLI client with root `bun run generate`.

**Scope** — In: provider-first service validation, route persistence/conflicts/placement, assignment review metadata, queued-review budget cancellation, preservation of existing failure notifications and generation. Out: DTO normalization (US-002), shared capability declarations (US-001), runner token/probe/execution/verdict work (US-004 through US-007), and web labels (US-008). CLI commands for reviews; the generated CLI client is regenerated but no command is added. Fleet analytics for `REVIEW` jobs; the analytics queries keep counting `RUN` and `PLAN` only. Automatic dispatch of reviews on new PR heads, per-repo auto-review settings and the auto-review switch; those are part B (feature `fleet-auto-review`).

**Interface** — `FleetJobsService.dispatch(actorId, projectId, dto, opts)`; `review?: { prNumber: number; botLogin: string }`; `review: { prNumber: prNumberOfReviewFeature(job.feature), botLogin: gitIdentity.name }`; `Error('invalid review feature')`.

userStories.title: The runner detects K0 and strips ambient identity variables
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prove nax's K0 review support before advertising it and isolate every nax invocation from inherited forge identity.

**Motivation** — `nax bot review` reviews a PR, remembers its own earlier findings and threads, and (nax feature `bot-forge-identity`, "K0") accepts a caller-supplied forge identity: `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE` (a file nax reads and deletes at startup) and `NAX_FORGE_LOGIN`.

**Approach** — Verbatim design requirements:
**K0 detection.** The runner reports `botReview: true` only when nax has `bot review` and honours the K0 contract: `<naxCommand> bot review --help` exits 0, and `<naxCommand> --version` run with `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN=probe` added to its environment exits 1 with stderr containing `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN is not supported`. A nax without K0 ignores that variable and exits 0. `NaxCli.run` gains a per-call `env` overlay for this. The static capability probe never reports `botReview`.

**Ambient forge-identity variables are stripped.** `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN`, `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE`, `NAX_FORGE_LOGIN` and `NAX_FORGE_USER_ID` join `CREDENTIAL_ENV_VARS`, so a value the daemon inherited never reaches any nax call (a K0 nax would refuse to start on an inherited `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN`). The `REVIEW` and probe overlays are applied after the strip.

- `CREDENTIAL_ENV_VARS` (`apps/runner/src/credentials/credential-env.ts:6`): adds the four `NAX_FORGE_*` names.
- `NaxCallOptions` / `createNaxCli` (`apps/runner/src/nax/nax-cli.ts`): `NaxCallOptions` gains `env?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>`, merged after `withoutCredentialVars(process.env)` and `NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR`.
- `FakeNaxCli` (`apps/runner/test/helpers/fake-nax-cli.ts`): records each call's `env`; by default answers `--version` with exit 0 whatever the env (a non-K0 nax) and `bot review --help` as an unknown command.
- Nax probe: adds `botReview: true` per call 3.

**Implementation connections** — Modify apps/runner/src/credentials/credential-env.ts, apps/runner/src/nax/nax-cli.ts, apps/runner/src/capabilities/nax-probe.ts and apps/runner/test/helpers/fake-nax-cli.ts; ensure apps/runner/src/capabilities/capability-probe.ts never reports botReview in static mode. Keep ordinary readNaxVersion startup/floor validation intact; the K0 call is a separate run with the deliberate env overlay. Record env in the fake and keep its default answers (`--version` exits 0 whatever the env, `bot review --help` is an unknown command), so every existing nax-probe spec keeps its exact report. Extend existing injected probe and nax-cli specs, including real-spawn env observation via a harmless fixture where appropriate; do not require installed nax.

**Scope** — In: ambient identity sanitation, explicit per-call env overlays, capability probing and fake call recording. Out: API capability parsing/placement (US-001), assignment/checkout/argv/restart (US-005), REVIEW job token-file injection (US-006), verdicts (US-007), and web labels (US-008). Installing nax with the `bot-forge-identity` feature on runner hosts; until it is installed, no runner reports `botReview` and `REVIEW` jobs stay queued.

**Interface** — `env?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>`; `NaxCli.run`; `botReview?: true`. The overlay is merged after `withoutCredentialVars(process.env)` and `NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR`.

userStories.title: The runner accepts, checks out and readopts a REVIEW
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry a validated REVIEW assignment through detached checkout, exact bot review argv construction and restart recovery without a PRD or status.json.

**Motivation** — The fleet design (§9.122, "S6 = K1 + K2") puts the review loop in koda: koda owns the bot identity (the `koda-fleet` App, whose key lives only in koda), triggers reviews, and later (K2) feeds project decisions in and stores review outcomes as memory.

**Approach** — Verbatim design requirements:
- `parseAssign` (`apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts:159`): accepts `REVIEW` with a `review` object (`prNumber` positive safe integer; `botLogin` 1..100 characters matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]*\[bot\]$`) and `bashMode` `raw`; rejects `REVIEW` without `review` (`bad('review')`), with another `bashMode` (`bad('bashMode')`), and `review` on any other command (`bad('review')`).
- Runner checkout: detached at the default branch's sha, no `prd.json` read, returned branch `null`.
- `prepareCheckout` (`apps/runner/src/executor/checkout.ts`): a `REVIEW` resolves `assign.ref`, checks out `--detach <sha>` and returns `{ ok: true, branch: null, refSha }`, before the `prd.json` read.
- Runner argv: `<naxCommand> bot review <prNumber> --profile <chain>` (the job profiles plus `koda-job-<jobId>`, joined with commas).
- `buildNaxArgv` (`executor/nax-process.ts`): `REVIEW` returns `[...naxCommand, 'bot', 'review', String(assign.review.prNumber), '--profile', chain]`.
- `Supervisor.readopt`: `REVIEW` joins the `PLAN` branch.

**Restart.** On readopt, a `REVIEW` takes the `PLAN` branch: watch it when the process is alive and ours, otherwise finish it (judge as above). It is never rejected for a missing `status.json`.

**Trust.** koda does not check PR authorship or forks; nax classifies the PR's trust itself.

**Implementation connections** — Modify apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts, apps/runner/src/executor/checkout.ts, apps/runner/src/executor/nax-process.ts and apps/runner/src/supervisor/supervisor.ts. Use the protocol review type introduced by US-001; clean and copy validated fields rather than retaining arbitrary input. Keep current profile/path validations, per-job profile marker and process-identity checks. Resolve REVIEW before PRD reads without changing PLAN's .nax check or RUN branch protection. Existing no-process-recorded, terminal, ASSIGNED, config and thread readopt behavior remains intact. Extend parser and Supervisor unit tests, argv tests and existing isolated real-git test/unit/checkout.spec.ts; no live forge is necessary.

**Scope** — In: REVIEW assignment validation, detached checkout, exact argv and PLAN-style readoption. Out: payload construction on the API (US-003), capability detection (US-004), token-file writing/spawn overlays (US-006) and final verdict/cost reporting (US-007). A cost cap enforced inside the review; nax `bot review` takes no cost flag, so `maxCostUsd` is not passed to nax.

**Interface** — `review?: { prNumber: number; botLogin: string }`; `prepareCheckout` returns `{ ok: true, branch: null, refSha }`; `buildNaxArgv` returns `[...naxCommand, 'bot', 'review', String(assign.review.prNumber), '--profile', chain]`; `Supervisor.readopt(jobId, leaseEpoch)`.

userStories.title: The runner starts a review with the token file
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Start REVIEW with the current job-scoped token in a mode-0600 disposable file and remove every runner-owned leftover.

**Motivation** — `nax bot review` reviews a PR, remembers its own earlier findings and threads, and (nax feature `bot-forge-identity`, "K0") accepts a caller-supplied forge identity: `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE` (a file nax reads and deletes at startup) and `NAX_FORGE_LOGIN`.

**Approach** — Verbatim design requirements:
**Token file (narrow exception to D88).** nax K0 rejects a login without a token file, and a GitHub App token cannot answer "who am I". For `REVIEW` only, the runner writes the job's current token to `<jobDir>/forge-token` (created with mode `0600`) and passes its path in `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE`. nax reads and deletes the file at startup; the runner removes a leftover when the spawn fails, at job cleanup, and in the attempt wipe. The token is never put in an environment variable or argv. The runner rule in `.nax/mono/apps/runner/context.md` ("A git token never goes to ... a file ...") already names this exception (amended on this branch before the run).

- Runner env: the stripped job env plus `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE=<jobDir>/forge-token` and `NAX_FORGE_LOGIN=<review.botLogin>`.
- `CredentialProvider` (`credentials/broker.ts`): adds optional `currentToken?(job: JobRow): string | null`; `CredentialBroker` implements it from `TokenCache.state(job.jobId, job.leaseEpoch, nowMs())`.
- New `apps/runner/src/executor/review-token.ts`: `REVIEW_TOKEN_FILE = 'forge-token'`; `writeReviewToken(jobDir, token): Promise<string>` creates `<jobDir>/forge-token` in one call with mode `0600` and returns its path; `removeReviewToken(jobDir): Promise<void>` removes it if present.
- `HostExecutorDeps` (`executor/host-executor.ts`): gains optional `spawnNax?` (default the module's `spawnNax`) so specs observe argv and env without starting a process.
- `HostExecutor.spawn`: for `REVIEW`, `credentials.currentToken?.(job)`; null or absent throws `Error('git token: none')` before any write or start; otherwise `writeReviewToken`, then start nax with the two env variables; if the start throws, `removeReviewToken` runs before the error propagates.
- `HostExecutor.cleanup`: calls `removeReviewToken(jobDir)`. `ATTEMPT_FILES` (`host-executor.ts:52`) adds `forge-token`.

`JobRun.prepareAndSpawn` maps a throw from `spawn` to `FAILED 'spawn failed: <message>'`.

**Failure handling** — The runner has no current token at spawn: `FAILED`, reason `spawn failed: git token: none`; nothing written, nax not started.

**Implementation connections** — Add review-token.ts and its co-located spec; modify credentials/broker.ts and executor/host-executor.ts. TokenCache.state must be queried for this exact job id and lease epoch using the broker clock; return null for any state other than a live token. Keep the existing credential shim and stripped job PATH/env behavior for all job kinds and apply REVIEW overlays after stripping. Never log/persist the token outside the narrow file exception or include it in an archive. File creation must be restricted in the write call, not chmod after a permissive write. Preserve finally-based cleanup of profiles, approvals and broker resources. Add forge-token to the existing attempt wipe before reuse. Extend HostExecutor tests with an injected spawnNax and fixed-token provider, real temp files and mode checks; exercise existing JobRun spawn-error mapping without depending on US-007 verdict changes.

**Scope** — In: current-token lookup, secure token-file helpers, REVIEW-only environment overlay, injected spawn seam and cleanup on failure/end/retry. Out: capability probes (US-004), assignment/argv/checkout/readopt (US-005), posted-review verdict and cost seam (US-007), and API assignment metadata (US-003). Refreshing the token during a review: the job token is minted at prepare and valid for an hour, so a review that runs past it fails at its next forge call. Fetching or storing the App bot's numeric user id; nax compares the injected login.

**Interface** — `currentToken?(job: JobRow): string | null`; `REVIEW_TOKEN_FILE = 'forge-token'`; `writeReviewToken(jobDir, token): Promise<string>`; `removeReviewToken(jobDir): Promise<void>`; optional `HostExecutorDeps.spawnNax?` defaults to the module's `spawnNax`.

userStories.title: The runner judges a review
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Derive REVIEW completion from nax's posted-review stdout marker, with cancellation precedence and ledger-based terminal cost.

**Motivation** — The fleet design (§9.122, "S6 = K1 + K2") puts the review loop in koda: koda owns the bot identity (the `koda-fleet` App, whose key lives only in koda), triggers reviews, and later (K2) feeds project decisions in and stores review outcomes as memory.

**Approach** — Verbatim design requirements:
**Verdict by nax's success line.** The runner has no nax exit code (nax runs detached), and nax writes `bot-review.json` before it posts, so the artifact alone does not mean the review posted. nax prints `nax bot review: artifact <path>` to stdout only when the review posted. A `REVIEW` is:
- `CANCELLED` when a cancel was requested (checked first);
- `COMPLETED` when `<jobDir>/nax.stdout` has a line starting `nax bot review: artifact `;
- otherwise `FAILED` with reason `review not posted`.
Ingesting the artifact into koda is K2.

In the following shared design paragraph, US-003 owns budget command inclusion; this story owns ledger reading and terminal cost reporting.

**Cost.** A `REVIEW` writes no `status.json`. The runner reports its cost from the nax cost ledger in `<outDir>` with the existing `readPlanCost`, as for `PLAN`. `REVIEW` joins `BUDGET_STOP_COMMANDS`, so a budget hard stop cancels queued reviews like `RUN` and `PLAN`.

- `JobExecutor` (`executor/job-executor.ts`): adds `readReviewPosted(job: JobRow): Promise<boolean>`; `HostExecutor` implements it with `reviewPosted(stdoutPath)` from the new `apps/runner/src/verdict/review-posted.ts`, true when the file has a line starting `nax bot review: artifact `, false when it has none or does not exist.
- `JobRun.judge` (`supervisor/job-run.ts:410`, private): a `REVIEW` branch beside `PLAN` returns the call-5 verdict and a snapshot whose `costSpentUsd` is `readPlanCost(job)` when defined; it never calls `readStatus`.

**Failure handling** — If nax wrote bot-review.json but did not post, the job is FAILED with reason review not posted. If nax never ran far enough to print the success line, the job is FAILED with reason review not posted.

**Implementation connections** — Create verdict/review-posted.ts and verdict/review-posted.spec.ts; modify executor/job-executor.ts, executor/host-executor.ts, supervisor/job-run.ts and test/helpers/fake-executor.ts. The fake `JobExecutor` gains a `readReviewPosted` that resolves `false` unless a test sets it, so every existing job-run spec keeps its behaviour. Read exactly <jobDir>/nax.stdout in HostExecutor. Place the REVIEW judge branch before the existing readStatus path; reuse readPlanCost and omit costSpentUsd if it is undefined. Preserve normal log draining, bundle upload, terminal snapshots and RUNNING -> UPLOADING -> terminal transitions. REVIEW must not call PLAN commit/push or RUN progress-push behavior. Drive the new verdict through JobRun with FakeExecutor rather than testing a private method alone; use real stdout files for the pure marker helper and extend HostExecutor tests for path wiring.

**Scope** — In: success-marker reader, executor seam/implementations/fake, verdict precedence and terminal cost reporting. Out: token delivery (US-006), restart routing (US-005), API budget command inclusion (US-003), and web labels (US-008). Ingesting `bot-review.json` into koda, passing project decisions to the review (`--decisions`), and storing review outcomes as memory; those are K2. A stderr tail in the failure reason of a `review not posted` job; the stderr log is still uploaded with the job.

**Interface** — `reviewPosted(stdoutPath)`; `readReviewPosted(job: JobRow): Promise<boolean>`; `readPlanCost(outDir)`; `JobRun.judge` returns the verdict and a snapshot whose `costSpentUsd` is `readPlanCost(job)` when defined.
